title: Primary Function
learningObjectives: Identify the structural role of a robot-arm link.
student: What structural function does the selected robot-arm link perform between adjacent joints?
instructor: The link positions the downstream joint and end effector while transferring forces and moments between joints.

title: External Loads
learningObjectives: Identify the assigned payload, self-weight, and torque.
student: Identify the payload force, link self-weight, and applied torsional moment acting on the idealized link. State where each acts.
instructor: The payload force acts vertically at the free end, link self-weight acts as a resultant at L/2, and the assigned pure torque acts about the longitudinal link axis.

title: Supports and Boundary Conditions
learningObjectives: Interpret the equivalent fixed upstream joint.
student: Identify the idealized support condition at the upstream joint and explain which translations and rotations it restrains.
instructor: The upstream joint is idealized as fully fixed, restraining all translations and rotations of the selected link at the root.

title: Load Path
learningObjectives: Trace bending and torque to the root.
student: Trace the load path from the end payload and joint torque through the link to the upstream joint. Identify where bending moment and torque are carried.
instructor: The payload and link weight create shear and bending carried through the link to the root. The drivetrain torque is transmitted about the link axis to the root restraint.

title: Critical Location
learningObjectives: Identify the fixed root as critical.
student: Before calculating stresses, identify the section expected to be critical and explain why.
instructor: The fixed/root section is critical because the bending moment is maximum there and the applied torque is transmitted through it.

title: Relevant Mechanical Responses
learningObjectives: Select bending, torsion, and von Mises stress.
student: Which stress components should be evaluated? Explain why axial stress, buckling, and connector stresses are not primary checks in the assigned model.
instructor: Evaluate bending normal stress, torsional shear stress, and their von Mises combination. The assigned idealization has no independent axial load, and it excludes buckling and connector mechanics.

title: Relevant Parameters
learningObjectives: Identify the seven editable variables and fixed gravity.
student: Identify the geometric, loading, and material parameters that control bending stress, torsional shear stress, and static-yield factor of safety.
instructor: The editable inputs are m_p, L, m_L, t, D_o, T, and S_y. Gravity is fixed at 9.81 m/s^2; D_i, c, I, J, resultants, stresses, and factor of safety are derived.

title: Student-Generated Structural Idealization
learningObjectives: Construct the cantilever and hollow-tube model.
student: Draw the link as an equivalent hollow circular cantilever. Show the fixed end, link length, payload force, self-weight resultant, applied torque, and critical root section.
instructor: A complete model shows the fixed root, payload at x = L, link-weight resultant at x = L/2, torque about the longitudinal axis, and the hollow circular section defined by D_o and t.

title: Modeling Assumptions
student: State the assumptions needed to replace the real robot link with the equivalent MEEN 305 model.
instructor: Assume a straight uniform hollow circular cantilever, fully fixed root, concentrated payload, midpoint self-weight resultant, pure axial torque, homogeneous isotropic material, static loading, and small deformation. The equivalent diameter is derived rather than photographed. Exclude local geometry, stress concentrations, sensors, joints, dynamics, impact, fatigue, buckling, connectors, and FEA.

title: Mechanics Analysis Plan
student: List the calculation sequence from external loading to root resultants, section properties, stress components, von Mises stress, factor of safety, and engineering assessment.
instructor: Calculate forces and root moments; derive D_i, c, I, and J; calculate bending and torsional stresses; combine them with von Mises; calculate n = S_y/sigma_VM; then assess the result and limitations.

title: Root Resultants
learningObjectives: Calculate payload and self-weight root bending.
student: Determine F_p, W_L, payload bending moment M_p, self-weight bending moment M_L, total root bending moment M, and root torque T.
instructor: F_p = m_p g = {{robot_link_Fp_N}} N; W_L = m_L g = {{robot_link_WL_N}} N; M_p = F_p L = {{robot_link_Mp_Nm}} N*m; M_L = W_L(L/2) = {{robot_link_ML_Nm}} N*m; M = M_p + M_L = {{robot_link_M_Nm}} N*m. The root torque is the assigned T.

title: Section Geometry
learningObjectives: Calculate derived section geometry and properties.
student: Calculate D_i, c, I, and J for the equivalent hollow circular section.
instructor: D_i = D_o - 2t = {{robot_link_Di_mm}} mm; c = D_o/2 = {{robot_link_c_mm}} mm; I = pi(D_o4-D_i4)/64 = {{robot_link_I_mm4}} mm4; J = pi(D_o4-D_i4)/32 = {{robot_link_J_mm4}} mm4.

title: Bending Stress
student: Calculate the maximum normal bending-stress magnitude at the critical root section.

title: Torsional Shear Stress
student: Calculate the maximum torsional shear stress at the outer surface of the critical root section.

title: Combined Stress
learningObjectives: Combine bending and torsion with von Mises.
student: At the outer-surface point where |sigma_b| is maximum, calculate the von Mises equivalent stress.

title: Strength Factor of Safety
student: Using the assigned yield strength, determine the static strength factor of safety n = S_y/sigma_VM.

title: Engineering Assessment
learningObjectives: Interpret the static check without overstating the model.
student: State whether the equivalent link passes the static-yield check, identify the dominant stress contribution, and recommend one direct mechanics-based change that would increase strength margin if required.
